clue.text: Far above sea level, hilltop is cultivated

parts.note: somewhere far above sea level is high up
the brow of a hill is its top

explanation.surface: A hilltop farm, high above the sea, has been put under the plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' suggests farming, but here it means refined and intellectual.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow person has refined, intellectual tastes, which is what cultivated means of a person.

clue.text: One military man leads every charge

indicators.note: the first pieces lead, going in front of the next word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP is a military policeman
every means each

explanation.surface: A soldier at the head of every charge into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a cavalry attack, but here it is a formal accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to charge them formally with misconduct.

clue.text: Uncompromising policies bring bad luck!

explanation.surface: Rigid politics bring misfortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough political positions are hard lines; the phrase is also a British exclamation of sympathy for misfortune.

clue.text: Prescription form

explanation.surface: A note from a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite prescribed by custom is a prescription for worship, and a fixed ceremony or procedure is a form.

clue.text: "I'm mixed up", cried the Welsh hypocrite

indicators.note: mixed letters are jumbled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A confused Welsh speaker calls out, admitting to being a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm mixed up' is the speech, but only 'up' and 'cried the Welsh' are fodder, with 'mixed' signalling the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical phrase (Matthew 23) describes someone fair outside but corrupt within, a hypocrite.

clue.text: Inexperienced heifer eats everything

indicators.note: the heifer takes something into its mouth, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a heifer is a young cow
everything means all

explanation.surface: A young farm animal, new to the world, devours whatever it finds.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow describes someone young and lacking worldly experience, a synonym.

clue.text: House-occupant in business set up interminable races

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so read backwards
having no end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a regatta is a series of boat races

explanation.surface: A homeowner in trade organising never-ending races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' cuts REGATTA to REGATT, and 'set up' turns it to TTAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottager is someone who lives in a cottage, a small house.

clue.text: Chicken in port

explanation.surface: Poultry at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Leghorn is a breed of domestic hen, and it is the old English name for Livorno, an Italian seaport.

clue.text: Sad without love, we get lost!

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so one word goes round another

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
begone is an old command meaning get lost

explanation.surface: Feeling down because love has gone, we have lost our way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so WE goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone means looking miserable and dejected.

clue.text: Stumbles around, having imbibed one drink

indicators.note: drinking something in puts one piece inside another
turned around means the word for stumbles is read backwards

parts.note: stumbles means trips
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone lurching about after a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns TRIPS into SPIRT, and 'having imbibed' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits such as whisky or gin are strong alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: One repeatedly mixed up with urgent affair

indicators.note: letters mixed up are jumbled into a new order
one taken repeatedly gives the numeral twice over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tangled up in a pressing matter, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles I to II, and 'mixed up' shuffles II with URGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrigue is a secret love affair or plot.

clue.text: Follow the spectators and drive too close

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match, a British usage

explanation.surface: Advice about shadowing a crowd of fans and driving dangerously.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the 'gate' is the attendance at a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailgating means driving right behind another vehicle, dangerously near its rear.

clue.text: A support at sea no longer

parts.note: a shore is a prop or beam that supports a wall

explanation.surface: A prop that has stopped working on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support at sea' reads as one phrase, but 'at sea no longer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on land has left the sea behind, being on dry ground by the coast.

clue.text: Some stretch in Asia

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run spanning them

explanation.surface: A remark about a part of the Asian continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'stretCH IN Asia', and the whole clue also describes the country, which is a stretch of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This country occupies a vast stretch of eastern Asia.

clue.text: No slouch when it comes to headgear!

definitions.text: No slouch when it comes to headgear!

parts.words: No slouch when it comes to headgear!
parts.note: a slouch hat has a soft drooping brim; the hat meant here is the opposite, its brim turned up stiffly

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who is good at choosing hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat has its brim turned up on two or three sides, unlike a slouch hat whose brim droops.

clue.text: Person ate artificial tongue

indicators.note: something artificial is made up, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ate a fake tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a constructed international language, and tongue means language.

clue.text: See 4 roaming free

indicators.note: letters roaming wander out of place into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 4 down, a ceremonial form

explanation.surface: Look at a ceremony wandering at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a cross-reference instruction, but its letters join RITUAL, the 4-down answer, as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at leisure is to be unoccupied, with free time.

clue.text: In favour of money in advance

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the pound is British money

explanation.surface: Supporting payment upfront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like an advance payment, but it means put forward an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound a theory is to put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: One enlisted to study handwriting

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
script is handwriting

explanation.surface: A recruit who signs up to study calligraphy.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscript is someone compulsorily enrolled into the armed forces.

clue.text: Advertisements in classified section

indicators.note: classified means sorted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Adverts in the classifieds part of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classified section' reads as the newspaper's small ads, but 'classified' sorts the letters of 'section'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notices are public announcements, such as adverts posted in a paper.

clue.text: Many like a bit of garlic

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
to love something is to like it a lot

explanation.surface: Lots of people enjoy a little garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one of the segments making up a bulb of garlic.

clue.text: Headstrong girl conceals name

indicators.note: the girl conceals a letter, holding it inside her name

parts.note: Violet is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wilful young woman keeps her name secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Both suggest forceful, uncontrolled behaviour; violent passions are headstrong and unrestrained.

clue.text: Press about to shed a little weight

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to shed weight is to lose it

indicators.note: only a little of the word is used, its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper about to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers or a squeeze, but a press is an old word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a cupboard for linen or clothes, a type of storage closet.

clue.text: Playing companion returned endlessly to net

indicators.note: something returned goes back, so the letters are read in the other direction
without its end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a partner is a companion in a game such as tennis or bridge

explanation.surface: A doubles partner keeps going back towards the net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'returned' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it, as a trap does.

clue.text: Sweet round tablet taken in water

indicators.note: turned round means the whole assembly is read backwards
one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a pool is a body of water
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: Swallowing a round tablet with water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' and 'round' together give POPILLOL turned backwards; 'round' looks like it describes the tablet's shape but reverses the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Temporary setback lands one county council in hock

indicators.note: one group of letters goes in another

parts.note: hough is a Scottish spelling of hock, the joint in an animal's hind leg
I is the Roman numeral for one
CC is the abbreviation for county council, a British local authority

explanation.surface: A local council lands in debt, a temporary problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hock' suggests debt, but hock is the leg joint, spelt HOUGH; this is the old spelling of hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is figuratively a small, passing problem or snag.

clue.text: Fresher going without one dish

indicators.note: doing without something means it is removed

parts.note: saucier means cheekier, fresher in manner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A first-year student skipping a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresher' looks like a British first-year student, but it means cheekier.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small shallow dish set under a cup.

clue.text: They even seemed to expect departmental heads to be examined

indicators.note: the heads of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Department chiefs were braced for scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads are T, E, S, T, E, D from 'They even seemed to expect departmental'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tested means put to the test, checked, which is examined.

clue.text: Taste shown in record request

indicators.note: one word appears inside another

parts.note: an entry is an item in a record or ledger
to eat is to taste food

explanation.surface: A request for tasting noted down in a record.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.
